question.prompt: On Monday, Millie puts a quart of seeds, \(25\%\) of which are millet, into a bird feeder. On each successive day she adds another quart of the same mix of seeds without removing any seeds that are left. Each day the birds eat only \(25\%\) of the millet in the feeder, but they eat all of the other seeds. On which day, just after Millie has placed the seeds, will the birds find that more than half the seeds in the feeder are millet?

solutions.explanation:
All the nonmillet seeds are eaten each day. Consequently, just after each new quart is added, there are exactly \(\frac34\) quart of nonmillet seeds. Millet makes up more than half of the feeder's contents exactly when its amount exceeds this \(\frac34\) quart.

Let \(M_n\) be the millet amount in quarts just after the seeds are added on day \(n\), with Monday as day \(1\). Initially \(M_1=\frac14\). The birds leave \(75\%=\frac34\) of that day's millet, and the next addition supplies another \(\frac14\) quart. Therefore
\[
M_{n+1}=\frac34M_n+\frac14.
\]
Applying this update gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Monday: }M_1&=\frac14<\frac34,\\
\text{Tuesday: }M_2&=\frac7{16}<\frac{12}{16},\\
\text{Wednesday: }M_3&=\frac{37}{64}<\frac{48}{64},\\
\text{Thursday: }M_4&=\frac{175}{256}<\frac{192}{256},\\
\text{Friday: }M_5&=\frac{781}{1024}>\frac{768}{1024}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The comparison fails on every earlier day and first holds on \(\boxed{\text{Friday}}\), choice D.
solutions.title: Track the millet each day
